Subject: PO requirements + invoice cadence question

Hi Rachel,

Quick procurement note as we're prepping the PO for Redwood: a couple of mandatory items from our side before we can route to AP. Please confirm that Redwood can support the following:

- PO number must appear in the invoice header and match the PO format: RMRK-<entity>-<6 digit>.
- We need to be able to accept split monthly invoicing against a single PO (we bill cost centers monthly).
- Preferred net terms are Net 90 for our enterprise customers; can Redwood accommodate Net 90?
- Please provide completed vendor form (we attached VendorForm_Rivermark.xlsx) and an updated SOW referencing the PO.
- For vendor setup we also need your tax ID and remittance instructions on the invoice.

Can you confirm feasibility and any consequences to pricing/discounting if we extend to Net 90?

Thanks,
Alejandro Cruz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Rivermark Health

Hi Alejandro — thanks for the heads up and for the vendor form. We're ready to support the PO header and split monthly invoicing, but I wanted to surface a few constraints from our finance side and propose a couple of options so we can align quickly:

1) PO on invoice header: yes — we will include the PO number exactly as provided (RMRK-...) and populate remittance/tax details on the invoice.

2) Split monthly invoices against a single PO: supported. We'll reference the PO and include a per-invoice line mapping to your cost-center identifier; we'll need the mapping table in the vendor form so invoices show the cost-center code.

3) Net terms (Net 90 request): our standard enterprise offering supports up to Net 60 after finance approval. Net 90 is outside standard policy and will require an AR/credit review. If Rivermark requires Net 90, we will need to:
   - Move pricing to the next discount band (we typically apply a 6% holdback on extended terms), OR
   - Take a longer commitment (12-month minimum term) with a consolidated PO covering the period so we can underwrite the receivable.

Proposed win-win (two paths):
A) Net 60 + monthly invoices = standard enterprise terms (no pricing change).
B) Net 90 + 12-month committed PO = we can keep current pricing but require the consolidated PO and a short credit form; Redwood will add a 30-day billing holdback reflected in our invoicing metadata.

I'll loop in finance (Vanessa & Vivek) to confirm the documentation they'd need. Also attaching an updated SOW that reflects monthly billing and the PO reference field.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_Rivermark_v2.pdf (PDF 190 KB)

Rachel / Vivek — quick internal note on the Rivermark ask.

- PO header + cost-center mapping: simple. We can populate custom invoice fields and include a cost-center line item on each invoice. We'll need the cost-center mapping table up front (spreadsheet).

- Net 90 ask: 
  * Our base position is Net 45 for new enterprise customers. Net 60 is acceptable with AR approval and an approved credit memo. Net 90 is permitted only with a) a signed 12-month commitment PO or b) an advance payment schedule for the first quarter.
  * If we agree to Net 90 without commitment, we put the account into an elevated credit review and apply a 4–6% discount holdback (this protects cash flow).

- Pricing impact: offering Net 90 in lieu of a 12-month committed PO will trigger the holdback and / or a 1.5% price increase for underwriting risk.

Suggest we present the two options Rachel outlined and call out the explicit tradeoffs: speed to PO (Net 60 standard) vs extended terms (Net 90 + commit OR Net 90 + pricing holdback).

If Rivermark pushes for Net 90, I can run a quick credit screen and estimate the holdback number by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
